questions.q: In SageMaker script mode, where does a scikit-learn training script find its training data channel?
options: In the SM_CHANNEL_TRAIN environment variable, a path to the channel directory
It must download the data from S3 itself using a hard-coded path
In the SM_MODEL_DIR environment variable
In a file named train.csv in the current working directory
questions.explain: Input channels are exposed as SM_CHANNEL_<NAME> variables (for example SM_CHANNEL_TRAIN and SM_CHANNEL_VALIDATION). SM_MODEL_DIR is where the model artifact must be written.

questions.q: Why did the capstone write a custom input_fn instead of relying on the container default?
options: Custom handlers are faster than defaults
The default handlers are not allowed for scikit-learn
SageMaker requires all four handlers to be custom
The default input_fn produces a NumPy array, but the pipeline needs named columns including a text plan column
questions.explain: The default deserializes CSV, JSON or NPY into a NumPy array. A pipeline with a ColumnTransformer on named columns needs a DataFrame, so a custom input_fn builds one.

questions.q: Why do the capstone's inference handlers deliberately reject application/xml requests with an error?
options: XML is not a valid data format anywhere
So callers learn what went wrong rather than receiving nonsense predictions
Because SageMaker endpoints refuse XML at the network layer
To reduce the cost of the endpoint
questions.explain: Explicit errors for unsupported content types make failures visible and debuggable.

questions.q: In the lesson's monitoring policy, week 2 had input drift flags but AUC of 0.805. What did the policy decide?
options: RETRAIN, because any drift means the model is broken
OK, because AUC is above 0.75
INVESTIGATE: input drift with acceptable quality
Delete the endpoint immediately
questions.explain: Input drift is a prompt to look closer; retraining is triggered by quality falling below the gate, which is the week 3 case.

questions.q: Which statement about the AWS code in this lesson is accurate?
options: It was run against a live AWS account and the outputs are shown
It is illustrative and adapted from the docs; SDK versions differ, so check current documentation
It works unchanged with every SageMaker SDK version
It is pseudocode with invented function names
questions.explain: No AWS account is available in this course, so the AWS calls are labeled illustrative. The local code (training, handlers, drift logic) was actually run.
